C2-16 | qwen3.8-27b | Prior claim that the promotion shim is load-bearing "in both thinking modes" was only true with --reasoning-parser qwen3-thinking attached — the parser routes the whole answer into reasoning_content even when thinking is off. Never tested: serving without a reasoning parser at all | No-shim path proven: built a --chat-template variant with the think-OFF empty- <think></think> prefill hardcoded, reasoning-instruction block stripped, --reasoning-parser dropped entirely. Replay PASS, finish=stop , reasoning_len=0 , 8 insights. E2E: succeeded, 3 discoveries, 120 s wall, direct connector to :30001 , judged 7/7 · Y — best qwen score of the campaign, zero proxy hops. Only keep the shim if a customer needs thinking-ON and thinking-OFF on the same running server. Unsloth's GGUF chat template ( unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF , embedded) was evaluated as an alternative base: its extras (merged system messages, developer role, tool-call validation) target message shapes AD never sends (Kibana emits exactly one user message, no system, no tools), and its enable_thinking toggle defaults to thinking-ON with the same client-field requirement as stock — so the hardcoded stock-based variant remains the measured recommendation. Generalization boundary (checked against each campaign model's template): the approach transfers only to models whose sole defect is a --reasoning-parser routing the answer out of content (qwen3-family serving configs). It does not apply to: GLM-4.7-Flash (toggle exists and a think-off template is buildable, but the measured thinking-OFF-alone mode rambles 97k chars with zero insights — guided-JSON response_format is a sampling constraint no template can express, shim stays mandatory), mistral-small-3.2/magistral (ctx-bound, not field-routing), gemma-4-31b ( enable_thinking|default(false) — think-OFF is already the template default, which is why it passed direct), gpt-oss-120b (already zero-config)

GLM-4.7-Flash — vendor recipe includes --reasoning-parser glm45 (we keep it, correct) + --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice (inert for AD — no tools API path) + --speculative-config.method mtp (not deployed — free perf left on the table). Magistral-Small-2509 — vendor recipe includes --reasoning-parser mistral as the default and only documented mode; [THINK]/[/THINK] tokens are core to the model with no thinking-off variant documented (unlike Qwen/GLM which support enable_thinking=false ). Our FAIL ( content_len=0 , 22,527/22,528 tokens on reasoning) is therefore not the same failure mode as the Qwen/GLM "hidden in reasoning field" bug — Kibana never received a complete thought to read. This is a reasoning model whose mandatory thinking mode structurally doesn't fit this corpus's context/output budget; the fix path is a larger ctx ceiling or a reasoning-promotion shim, not stripping a parser that per vendor docs may have no off switch

Verdict: base models stay — no derivative is better optimized for this use case; survey recorded so it is not relitigated
